synthesis:draft.headline: Peak SA1 RRP 4981.0 $/MWh at interval ending 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST (2026-07-30T16:35:00Z)
summary: Peak 5-minute RRP in SA1 was 4981.0 $/MWh at interval ending 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST (2026-07-30T16:35:00Z).
The project analysis threshold was 300.0 $/MWh and 214 five-minute intervals met-or-exceeded that threshold in the window.

Dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the 5-minute peak interval was 1472.82 MW (dispatch TOTALDEMAND); the half-hour operational demand containing the peak (half-hour ending 2026-07-30T17:00:00Z) was 1466.0 MW and the window maximum operational demand was 2173.0 MW.
Net interchange at the peak interval was -82.59 MW (net flow into SA1, import).
SCADA-observed unit output changes in the broader window include -112.0 MW (TORRB3), -109.0 MW (TORRB2), -86.22 MW (BARKIPS) and -75.55 MW (QPS5).
Point weather summary for Adelaide shows WS50M wind speed max 3.5 m/s and min 1.24 m/s in the retrieved window.
AEMO published a market notice reporting a non-credible contingency event in SA and stating "The cause of this non credible contingency event is not known at this stage." [c1]

possible_explanations.statement: Wind generation might have been low around the spike and might have contributed to tight supply; testing requires wind-generation SCADA or aggregated wind output with timestamps and comparison to forecasts.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve unit-level generation time series for wind farms (labelled by fuel) covering 16:00–17:00 UTC with evidence ids, and compare to pre-dispatch/forecast wind generation for the same intervals (forecast evidence ids).

possible_explanations.statement: Large reductions in individual unit outputs might have reduced available dispatchable capacity and might be relevant to the price spike.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve continuous unit-level dispatch-generation time series and availability/outage records for the named units across 15:30–17:00 UTC (evidence ids) and check timing relative to the 16:35 UTC spike.

possible_explanations.statement: Interconnector limits, constraints or local network events might have tightened supply locally (the window includes a market notice about a non-credible contingency event) [c1].
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Fetch interconnector limit/outage notices, constraint-set invocations and constraint binding records for the relevant intervals (evidence ids), and compare net interchange and constraint binding at 16:35 UTC.

possible_explanations.statement: Offer or rebid behaviour might have placed high-priced offers or scarcity-priced offers into dispatch and might explain the extreme price.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve bid/offer and rebid data for the interval(s) around 16:35 UTC with evidence ids and check for priced offers or rebids that coincided with the spike.

citations.quote: The cause of this non credible contingency event is not known at this stage.
citations.supports: AEMO market notice reporting a non-credible contingency event in SA on 2026-07-30

uncertainties: No unit-level generation series labelled by fuel (wind vs non-wind) was returned for the exact spike interval, so wind output at 16:35 UTC is not directly evidenced.
SCADA change observations do not identify causes (trip, dispatch change, bidding) and do not by themselves show whether reductions in output were forced outages or scheduled changes.
missing_evidence: Unit-level generation time series with fuel-type labels (wind farm aggregated SCADA) for 15:30–17:00 UTC with evidence ids.
Hourly or sub-hourly WS50M wind-speed value with an evidence id at the spike interval(s) (around 16:35 UTC).
Unit availability/forced outage records and rebid/offer data for the interval(s) around the spike with evidence ids.
Constraint binding records, interconnector limit/outage notices and invoked constraint sets for the interval(s) around 16:35 UTC with evidence ids.
